paragraphs: Gogo Inc. ("Gogo", the "Company", "we" or "us") is the only multi-orbit, multi-band in-flight connectivity provider offering connectivity technology purpose-built for business and military/government aviation. We have a holistic approach of providing broadband connectivity services to our customers from small to large aircraft and heavy jets through our air-to-ground ("ATG") technology and integrated low earth orbit ("LEO") and geostationary earth orbit ("GEO") satellite solutions provided by multiple satellite constellations owned by our satellite network partners. We aim to deliver to our customers consistent, global tip-to-tail connectivity with a suite of software, hardware, and advanced infrastructure supported by a 24/7/365 in-person customer support team to fit their every need.

By leveraging our multi-orbit, multi-band in-flight connectivity solutions, our global footprint, including a mature sales force and technical support, we can provide our customers with essential market access, speed, bandwidth, greater reliability, redundancy, and responsiveness that they need around the world. Our connectivity solutions are used by business and military/government aviation customers in over 100 countries, many of which view our products and services as critical to their daily operations and integral to their communications and business infrastructure. We also serve our growing military/government customer base by providing cost-effective, turnkey in-flight connectivity that integrates innovative, commercially proven technologies and software to deliver mission-tailored capabilities.

We believe that, with our innovative solutions and tailored customer service, we are well-positioned to compete in the evolving in-flight connectivity market, which is undergoing significant change driven by several catalysts. The most significant technological advancement that is driving change in our industry today is the introduction of LEO satellite technology, which provides, among other things, a global service offering, higher capacity, and lower latency than currently available alternatives. Further, we believe that demand for in-flight connectivity will continue to increase because of changes in the demographics of our customer base, the proliferation of social applications, and lifestyle changes that remain in a post-COVID world, such as videoconferencing and live streaming.

On December 3, 2024 (the "Closing"), we purchased all of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Satcom Direct, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (f/k/a Satcom Direct, Inc., a Florida corporation) and certain of its affiliates and subsidiaries (collectively, "Satcom Direct"), in exchange for (i) an aggregate cash purchase price of approximately $375,000,000, subject to customary post-closing adjustments, (ii) 5,000,000 restricted shares of the Company's common stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the "Common Stock") (valued at approximately $40,500,000 based on the Company's closing stock price of $8.10 on December 2, 2024), and (iii) up to an additional $225,000,000 in potential earnout payments of cash and/or Common Stock tied to realizing certain financial performance milestones over four years following the Closing.

Our business strategy is to be a global satellite network integrator and facilitator by developing innovative technological and business solutions addressing the specific needs of our business and military/government customers – making connectivity accessible, available, and secure worldwide. Our technological expertise and deep understanding of the in-flight connectivity market, built over decades of leadership in our industry, places us in a prime position for continued growth over the coming decade.
The following are the primary solutions that enable us to pursue our strategy:

• Gogo Galileo: We commercially launched the first global LEO broadband satellite service purpose-built for business aviation ("Gogo Galileo") in the first quarter of 2025. Gogo Galileo uses an electronically steered antenna ("ESA"), specifically designed with Hughes Network Systems, LLC ("Hughes") to address a broad range of business aviation and military/government aircraft, operating on a LEO satellite network operated by Network Access Associates, Ltd. ("Eutelsat OneWeb"). We believe that Gogo Galileo, in combination with or as an alternative to our ATG and GEO services, will allow us to penetrate the North American market and provide an upgrade path and an additional product for our existing ATG and GEO customer base. In addition, we believe that Gogo Galileo will allow us to penetrate the business aviation and military/government markets outside of North America, where there has been a lower adoption rate of in-flight connectivity. The launch of Gogo Galileo augments our combined product and service offerings for ATG broadband, GEO broadband, and narrowband satellite services, as described below.

• ATG Broadband Service: Gogo is the leading provider of in-flight connectivity in the ATG broadband market in North America. Gogo started in analogue ATG technology in the late 1990s, then, as analogue cellular backhaul disappeared, migrated to narrowband satellite connectivity in the early 2000s, and then back to ATG with our digital broadband networks beginning in 2010. We continue to augment our ATG broadband connectivity services through the addition of our fourth ATG broadband network (Gogo 5G), which we launched in the fourth quarter of 2025. We are also actively

working with a subset of our customers utilizing our AVANCE products and legacy Gogo Biz ATG airborne system to transition to an AVANCE system compatible with a new LTE network. We anticipate this subset of customers will see improved performance because of this network transition, which is expected to occur in 2026. The cost for the transition to the new LTE network is offset by our participation in the FCC Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program (the "FCC Reimbursement Program").

• GEO Broadband Service: We partner with industry satellite network operators to deliver GEO Ku- and Ka-band services. Our combined product offerings allow us to integrate and offer network agnostic solutions, providing customers with GEO satellite services utilizing networks provided by operators, including, among others, SES S.A. ("SES") and Viasat, Inc. ("Viasat").

• Narrowband Satellite Services: Since our initial migration to narrowband satellite connectivity in the early 2000s, we continue to provide narrowband satellite services to customers in North America and internationally. We now provide this narrowband satellite service through reseller agreements with satellite providers, including Iridium Satellite LLC ("Iridium") and Viasat.

As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 1,321 activated GEO broadband business aviation customer aircraft and 6,402 line-replaceable units ("LRUs") for our ATG broadband services, of which approximately 4,956 were equipped with AVANCE.

We accomplish our mission as the world's only multi-orbit, multi-band in-flight connectivity provider, by delivering secure and reliable in-flight connectivity solutions for business and military/government aviation customers, and by offering a comprehensive portfolio of products and services consisting of our in-flight systems, in-flight services, aviation partner support, engineering, design and development services, and production operations functions.

In-Flight Systems. Across both our business aviation and military/government customer bases, our customers have a broad range of equipment choices for their in-flight systems, which allows us to provide a solution based on geography, mission, size of aircraft and passenger preference. Customers can select a variety of different products such as our AVANCE platforms, Gogo Galileo, Plane Simple®, Satcom Direct Router ("SDR"), SD PRO®, FlightDeck Freedom, and other products to fit their needs.

paragraphs: You should consider and read carefully all of the risks and uncertainties described below, as well as other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and related notes. The risks described below are not the only ones facing us. The occurrence of any of the following risks or additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. This Annual Report on Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements and estimates that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of specific factors, including the risks and uncertainties described below.

Our business is dependent on our ability to continuously attract and retain users of our connectivity and other service offerings, and we cannot be certain that we will be successful in these efforts or that customer retention levels will not materially decline. For the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, the service we provided (which excludes service provided on commercial aircraft under an ATG network sharing agreement with Intelsat) generated approximately 84%, 80%, and 78% of our revenue from operations, respectively. A significant portion of such service revenue is generated through individual subscription agreements with our customers that cover a single or small number of aircraft, with the remainder generated through subscription agreements with certain fractional or charter operators covering larger fleets of aircraft. These agreements are generally between one and three years in duration but can be longer. As such, we have no assurance that any of such customers will renew their existing agreements with us upon expiration on comparable terms or at all, including as a result of a lack of demand or dissatisfaction with our services or the availability of superior or less expensive alternatives in the market. To the extent that our subscribers terminate or fail to renew their contracts with us for any reason, our business prospects, financial condition and results of operations may be materially adversely affected.
We have in the past, and may in the future, experience periods of reduced usage of our services by our customers, which could adversely impact our results of operations and profitability.

Revenue from equipment sales accounted for approximately 15%, 18%, and 20% of our revenue for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively. More than 90% of our equipment revenue in each such fiscal year was generated from contracts with OEMs and after-market dealers. Almost all of our contracts with OEMs and dealers are terminable at will by either party on short notice. If one or more key OEMs or dealers terminates its relationship with us for any reason or our contract expires and is not renewed, our business and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected. In addition, pursuant to many of our contracts with our OEM distribution partners, we have agreed to deliver equipment and/or services, including equipment and services not yet in production, for a fixed price and, accordingly, take the risk of any cost overruns or delays in the completion of the design and manufacturing of the product. Certain of our contracts with our OEMs also include provisions that, under specified circumstances, entitle them to the benefit of certain more favorable provisions than included in other equipment contracts, including with respect to pricing. These provisions, some of which have retroactive effect, may limit the benefits we realize from contracts containing such provisions. Our inability to identify and offer improved terms to a distribution partner or customer in accordance with such a provision could negatively affect our relationship with that distribution partner or customer or give rise to a claim that we are in breach of such contract.

Many of our distribution partners have also not committed to purchase any minimum quantity of our equipment. In certain cases, we must anticipate the future volume of orders based upon non-binding production schedules provided by OEMs, historical purchasing patterns and informal discussions with customers and dealers as to their anticipated future requirements. Cancellations, reductions or delays by OEMs and dealers may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Our distribution partners may be materially adversely impacted by economic downturns and market disruptions. See "—Adverse economic conditions, including economic slowdowns, and geopolitical instability may have a material adverse effect on our business." In anticipation of changing economic conditions, OEMs in particular may be more conservative in their production, which may reduce our market opportunities. Further, unfavorable market conditions could cause one or more of our OEMs or dealers to file for bankruptcy, which may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

These forward-looking statements are subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, including, but not limited to, the risks and uncertainties described under "Risk Factors" in this report. Our fiscal year ends December 31 and, unless otherwise noted, references to years or fiscal are for fiscal years ended December 31. See "— Results of Operations."

The Company is the only multi-orbit, multi-band in-flight connectivity provider offering connectivity technology purpose-built for business and military/government aviation. We have a holistic approach of providing broadband connectivity services to our customers from small to large aircraft and heavy jets through our ATG technology and integrated LEO and GEO satellite solutions provided by multiple satellite constellations owned by our satellite network partners. We aim to deliver to our customers consistent, global tip-to-tail connectivity with a suite of software, hardware, and advanced infrastructure supported by a 24/7/365 in-person customer support team to fit their every need.

Our Company's chief operating decision maker ("CODM"), who is the Chief Executive Officer, makes resource and operating decisions by evaluating the performance and business results on a consolidated basis. As we do not have multiple segments, we do not present segment information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We believe that our operating and business performance is driven by various factors that affect the business and military/government aviation industries, including trends affecting the travel industry and trends affecting the customer bases that we target, as well as factors that affect wireless Internet service providers and general macroeconomic factors. Key factors that may affect our future performance include:

• our ability to implement on a timely basis and costs associated with the ongoing implementation of our technology roadmap, including installation of and/or upgrades to the ATG Broadband technologies we currently offer, Gogo 5G, Gogo Galileo, LTE and any other next generation or other new technology that we develop or acquire;

• our ability to manage issues and related costs that may arise in connection with the implementation of our technology roadmap, including technological issues and related remediation efforts and technological shifts, failures or delays on the part of antenna, chipset, and other equipment developers and providers or satellite network providers, some of which are single-source;
• our ability to license additional spectrum and make other improvements to our ATG network and operations as technology and user expectations change;
• the number of aircraft in service in our markets, including consolidations or changes in fleet size by one or more of our large-fleet customers;
• the economic environment and other trends that affect both business and leisure aviation travel;
• disruptions to supply chains in the aviation industry and installations of our equipment driven by, among other things, labor shortages;

• the extent of our customers' adoption of our products and services, which is affected by, among other things, willingness to pay for the services that we provide, the quality and reliability of our products and services, changes in technology and competition from current competitors and new market entrants;
• our ability to engage suppliers of equipment components and network services on a timely basis and on commercially reasonable terms;

paragraphs: Gogo Inc. ("Gogo", the "Company", "we" or "us") 為唯一提供多軌道、多頻段機上連線服務的公司，其連線技術專為商業與軍事/政府航空用途設計。我們以整體性的方式為客戶提供寬頻連線服務，從小型飛機到大型飛機與重型噴氣機，透過我們的空對地 ("ATG") 技術與整合低軌道 ("LEO") 與地球同步軌道 ("GEO") 衛星解決方案，這些解決方案由我們衛星網路夥伴所擁有之多個衛星星座提供。我們的目標是為客戶提供一致、全球性的端到端連線服務，搭配一套軟體、硬體與先進基礎設施，並由 24/7/365 的現場客戶支援團隊提供服務，以符合客戶的各種需求。

透過運用我們的多軌道、多頻段機上連線解決方案、全球佈局，包括成熟的銷售團隊與技術支援，我們能為客戶提供市場准入、速度、頻寬、更高的可靠性、備用系統與反應速度，以應對全球各地的需要。我們的連線解決方案被用於商業與軍事/政府航空客戶於超過 100 個國家，許多國家將我們的產品與服務視為日常運作的關鍵，並與其通訊與業務基礎設施息息相關。我們也透過提供成本效益高、一站式機上連線服務來服務我們日益成長的軍事/政府客戶羣，這些服務整合創新、已商業驗證的技術與軟體，以提供符合任務需求的解決方案。
我們相信，憑藉我們的創新解決方案與個性化客戶服務，我們在演進中的機上連線市場中處於優勢地位，該市場正因多種因素而經歷重大變革。目前推動產業變革最重要的技術進步是低軌道衛星技術的引入，該技術提供全球服務方案、更高的容量與更低的延遲，這遠優於現有替代方案。此外，我們相信機上連線的需求將持續增加，這是因為客戶羣體的結構變化、社交應用的普及，以及後疫情時代的生活方式改變，例如視訊會議與即時串流。

於 2024 年 12 月 3 日 ("交易完成日")，我們購入 Satcom Direct, LLC，一家特拉華州有限責任公司 (原為 Florida 州公司 Satcom Direct, Inc.) 及其部分附屬公司與子公司 (合稱 "Satcom Direct") 的所有已發行及流通的權益，對價為 (i) 約 375,000,000 美元現金購入價格，扣除常規的交易後調整，(ii) 5,000,000 限制性發行的本公司普通股，每股面值 0.0001 美元 ("普通股") (根據本公司於 2024 年 12 月 2 日收市股價 8.10 美元計算，價值約 40,500,000 美元)，以及 (iii) 最多 225,000,000 美元的潛在 earnout 支付，以現金與/或普通股形式支付，與實現特定財務績效里程碑有關，時間為交易完成日後四年。
我們的業務策略是成為全球衛星網路整合商與促進者，透過開發創新技術與商業解決方案，以應對我們商業與軍事/政府客戶的特定需求 – 讓連線在全球範圍內變得可及、可用且安全。我們的技術專業與對機上連線市場的深入瞭解，經過數十年在產業中的領導地位，使我們在未來十年內持續成長的優勢位置。
以下為我們執行策略的主要解決方案：

• Gogo Galileo：我們於 2025 年第一季商業啟動全球低軌道 ("LEO") 寬頻衛星服務，專為商業航空設計 ("Gogo Galileo")。Gogo Galileo 使用電子導向天線 ("ESA")，特別與 Hughes Network Systems, LLC ("Hughes") 合作設計，以應對廣泛的商業航空與軍事/政府飛機，運行於由 Network Access Associates, Ltd. ("Eutelsat OneWeb") 管理的低軌道衛星網路。我們相信 Gogo Galileo，與我們的 ATG 與 GEO 服務結合或作為替代方案，將使我們能夠進入北美市場，並為現有的 ATG 與 GEO 客戶提供升級路徑與額外產品。此外，我們相信 Gogo Galileo 將使我們能夠進入北美以外的商業航空與軍事/政府市場，這些市場在機上連線的採用率較低。Gogo Galileo 的啟動增強了我們在 ATG 寬頻、GEO 寬頻與窄頻衛星服務方面的產品與服務組合，如後文所述。

• ATG 寬頻服務：Gogo 是北美機上連線市場中寬頻 ATG 服務的領導者。Gogo 於 1990 年代末開始使用類比 ATG 技術，當類比蜂巢式回程技術消失後，於 2000 年代初期轉向窄頻衛星連線，並於 2010 年開始重新使用 ATG 並推出我們的數位寬頻網路。我們持續透過增加第四個 ATG 寬頻網路 (Gogo 5G)，於 2025 年第四季啟動，來強化我們的 ATG 寬頻連線服務。我們也積極

與部分客戶合作，利用我們的 AVANCE 產品及 legacy Gogo Biz ATG 空中系統，轉型至與新 LTE 網路相容的 AVANCE 系統。我們預期這部分客戶會因這項網路轉型而看到表現改善，預計將於 2026 年發生。轉型至新 LTE 網路的成本，因我們參與 FCC Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Reimbursement Program (the "FCC Reimbursement Program") 而獲得補償。
• GEO Broadband Service: 我們與產業衛星網路運營商合作，提供 GEO Ku- 和 Ka-band 服務。我們的整合性產品組合使我們能提供網路無關的解決方案，讓客戶透過運營商提供的網路，取得 GEO 衛星服務，包括但不限於 SES S.A. ("SES") 和 Viasat, Inc. ("Viasat")。
• Narrowband Satellite Services: 自我們在 2000 年初期轉型至窄頻衛星連線以來，我們持續為北美洲及國際客戶提供窄頻衛星服務。我們現在透過與衛星供應商的經銷協議提供此窄頻衛星服務，包括 Iridium Satellite LLC ("Iridium") 和 Viasat。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們約有 1,321 架已啟動的 GEO 寬帶商務航空客戶飛機，以及 6,402 個線可更換單元 ("LRUs") 用於我們的 ATG 寬帶服務，其中約 4,956 個裝備了 AVANCE。
我們透過提供商務及軍事/政府航空客戶安全且可靠的機上連線解決方案，以及提供包含我們機上系統、機上服務、航空夥伴支援、工程、設計與開發服務，以及生產作業功能的完整產品與服務組合，實現我們作為全球唯一多軌道、多頻段機上連線服務供應商的使命。

In-Flight Systems. 在我們的商務航空與軍事/政府客戶羣中，客戶對機上系統的設備選擇有廣泛的範疇，這使我們能根據地理、任務、飛機規模及乘客偏好，提供符合需求的解決方案。客戶可選擇多種不同產品，例如我們的 AVANCE 平台、Gogo Galileo、Plane Simple®、Satcom Direct Router ("SDR")、SD PRO®、FlightDeck Freedom，以及其他產品以符合其需求。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析旨在協助讀者瞭解本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果、流動性及資本資源。請配合閱讀本年度報表 10-K 所附之合併財務報表及相關附註內容。
本討論中關於產業展望、本公司對未來營運表現、流動性及資本資源之預期，以及其他非歷史性陳述，均屬未來展望性陳述。這些未來展望性陳述受許多風險與不確定性影響，包括但不限於本報告中「風險因素」部分所描述之風險與不確定性。本公司實際結果可能與未來展望性陳述所載或暗示之內容有重大差異。
本公司會計年度為 12 月 31 日，除非另有說明，否則提及年份或會計年度均指截至 12 月 31 日之會計年度。請參閱「— 營運成果」。

本公司為唯一提供多軌道、多頻段機上連線服務之供應商，其連線技術專為商務與軍事/政府航空產業設計。本公司以整體方式為客戶提供寬頻連線服務，從小型飛機至大型飛機及重型飛機，透過本公司之 ATG 技術及整合 LEO 與 GEO 衛星解決方案，由多個衛星星座所有者之衛星網路夥伴提供。本公司目標是為客戶提供一致、全球性的端到端連線服務，搭配一套軟體、硬體及先進基礎設施，並由 24/7/365 現場客戶支援團隊支援，以符合客戶各項需求。
本公司之主要營運決策者（「CODM」），即首席執行長，透過評估整體營運表現與業務成果，做出資源與營運決策。由於本公司並無多個應報告分部，因此本年度報表 10-K 中未提供分部資訊。
本公司認為，營運與業務表現受多種因素影響，包括影響商務與軍事/政府航空產業之因素，以及影響旅客產業與本公司目標客戶羣之趨勢，以及影響無線互聯網服務供應商與總體經濟之因素。可能影響本公司未來表現之關鍵因素包括：
• 本公司能否及時執行並處理與持續執行技術路線圖相關之成本，包括安裝及/或升級現有之 ATG 寬頻技術、Gogo 5G、Gogo Galileo、LTE 及任何其他新世代或新技術之開發或取得；
• 本公司能否管理與技術路線圖執行相關之問題與相關成本，包括技術問題及相關解決措施、技術變遷、設備開發商與供應商或衛星網路供應商之失敗或延誤，部分供應商為單一來源；
• 我們取得額外頻譜許可及對 ATG 網路與營運進行其他改進的能力，隨著科技與用戶期望的變化；
• 我們市場中在役飛機數量，包括因合併或大型機隊客戶 fleet size 變動所導致的變化；
• 經濟環境及其他影響商務與休閒航空旅行的趨勢；
• 航空產業供應鏈中斷，以及因勞動力短缺等因素導致我們設備安裝的影響；
• 我們客戶採用我們產品與服務的程度，此程度受諸如願意為我們提供的服務付費、我們產品與服務的品質與可靠性、科技變更及現有競爭對手與新市場參與者的競爭等因素影響；
• 我們能否及時以商業合理條件聘請設備零組件與網路服務供應商；

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們可能無法持續從提供連線及其它服務方案中產生收入，這可能會對我們的業務及獲利造成重大且不利的影響。
我們的設備銷售依賴於我們的關鍵OEMs及經銷商。
我們依賴第三方衛星網路供應商，這些供應商為單一來源供應商，來提供我們的衛星服務。
我們依賴第三方，其中許多為單一來源供應商，來製造設備零組件、為我們的網路提供服務，以及安裝與維護我們的設備。
競爭可能會導致價格下降、收入減少及市場地位喪失，並可能對我們的營運成果造成損害。
我們的開發契約可能對我們而言難以遵守，並可能使我們面臨第三方損害賠償的聲請，我們可能因固定價格契約而產生損失。
我們參與美國政府契約，使我們面臨顯著的商業及其他業務風險。
本公司參與非美國政府契約，使我們面臨重大風險。
衛星具有有限的使用壽命，其實際運作壽命可能短於其任務壽命。
全球供應鏈挑戰與物流問題以及通貨膨脹的增加，已對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生，且可能持續產生不利影響。
我們面臨與國際營運相關的多種風險，這些風險可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
本公司業務面臨外幣風險。
隨著我們在地理上擴張及其他方面發展，我們可能遇到維持企業文化的困難，且業務、營運成果及財務狀況可能因此受到不利影響。
我們可能無法招募、培訓及留住維持競爭力及執行成長策略所必需的高技能員工。我們關鍵人員的流失可能對業務造成損害。
疫情或其他傳染病的爆發以及為對抗這些疫情所實施的措施，已對我們的業務產生，且可能持續產生重大不利影響。
不利的經濟情勢，包括經濟成長放緩，以及國際政治局勢不穩定，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能無法完全運用部分遞延所得稅資產，這將對本公司獲利及其他綜合收入造成負面影響。
本公司可能因全球氣候變遷及其他永續相關議題而受到不利影響。
本公司可能無法成功評估或追求戰略機會，這可能會對本公司營業收入、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。
與本公司科技及智慧財產權相關的風險
本公司最近部署的 Gogo 5G 及 Gogo Galileo 服務可能無法在市場中有效競爭，或面臨與實作相關的問題。
本公司業務依賴於頻譜的可用性。
未來可能有額外的 ATG 頻譜，無論為授權或未授權，可供使用或可能可供使用。
本公司或其第三方供應商或服務提供者若遭遇服務中斷，可能會定期且未來也可能遭受不利影響
paragraphs: 您應仔細考慮並閱讀下列所有風險與不確定性，以及本年度報表（Form 10-K）中包含的其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關附註。下列所描述的風險並非我們唯一面臨的風險。上述任何風險或目前尚未知悉的其他風險與不確定性，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。本年度報表（Form 10-K）亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的預測性陳述與估計。我們的實際結果可能與預測性陳述中所預期的有重大差異，原因包括下列所描述的風險與不確定性。

我們的業務依賴於我們持續吸引並留住使用我們連線服務及其他服務方案的用戶，我們無法確定我們是否會成功進行這些努力，或用戶留存率不會大幅下降。截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日的會計年度，我們所提供的服務（排除根據與Intelsat的ATG網路共享協議所提供的商業飛機服務）分別約佔我們營業收入的84%、80%及78%。這些服務收入的大部分來自與客戶簽訂的個別訂閱協議，這些協議涵蓋單一或少量飛機，其餘則來自與某些分級或包機運營商簽訂的訂閱協議，涵蓋較大的飛機機隊。這些協議通常為一至三年，但可能更長。因此，我們無法保證任何客戶在協議到期時會以相同條件或任何條件續約，包括因需求不足或對我們的服務不滿意，或市場上存在更優或更便宜的替代方案所致。若我們的用戶因任何原因終止或未續約與我們的契約，可能對我們的業務前景、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
我們過去曾經驗過，也可能未來會經驗客戶使用我們服務的用量減少，這可能會對我們的營運成果及獲利造成不利影響。

設備銷售所產生的收入約佔我們在截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日會計年度的營業收入的15%、18%及20%。在每個會計年度中，我們超過90%的設備收入來自與OEMs及經銷商簽訂的契約。我們與OEMs及經銷商的大多數契約均可由任一方在短時間內終止。若一個或多個關鍵OEMs或經銷商因任何原因終止與我們的關係，或契約到期且未續約，可能對我們的業務及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。此外，根據我們與OEM分銷夥伴的許多契約，我們同意以固定價格交付設備及/或服務，包括尚未投入生產的設備及服務，因此我們需承擔任何成本超支或設計與製造產品完成時間延誤的風險。我們與部分OEMs的契約亦包含條款，根據特定情況，這些OEMs可享有比其他設備契約中包含的更優惠條款的權益，包括價格方面。這些條款，其中一些具有追溯效力，可能限制我們從包含這些條款的契約中獲得的效益。我們若無法根據這些條款與分銷夥伴或客戶識別並提供更優的條件，可能對與該分銷夥伴或客戶的關係造成負面影響，或導致我們被認為違反契約。
我們的分銷夥伴亦未承諾購買我們設備的最低數量。在某些情況下，我們必須根據OEMs提供的非綁定生產排程、歷史採購模式及與客戶及經銷商的非正式討論，預測未來的訂單數量。OEMs及經銷商的取消、減少或延遲訂單，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
我們的分銷夥伴可能因經濟衰退及市場動盪而受到重大不利影響。請參閱「—不利的經濟條件，包括經濟減速，以及地緣政治不穩定可能對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。」為應對經濟條件的變化，OEMs尤其可能更加保守地進行生產，這可能減少我們的市場機會。此外，不利的市場條件可能導致我們的OEMs或經銷商提出破產保護，這可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。
